about: The auto-anatomist thread's gold tier 3 annealer screen, as data for the shared flowchart page (PIPE runs and N steps). Flow kind autoanatomist, class AutoanatomistFlow, gate word `autoanatomist <plan>`, driver grid/autoanatomist.sbatch, PREREG docs/research/autoanatomist-screen/PREREG.md, all on SchwingNet PR 483, none landed yet.

aa_plan.title: Plan and split
aa_plan.short: Which CTs, which part each person is in, which trial this task is.
aa_plan.does: Reads the plan file and the gold 3 store's ENHANCE.PET rows (CT and label map). Puts each person in train, validation or test by the project's frozen hash rule, and keeps a fixed subset by a second hash. Never reads a test person.
aa_plan.reads: grid/screens/gold3_latent_screen.json (or gold3_latent_smoke.json); data/splits/rule.json; the gold 3 store's rows on the grid
aa_plan.writes: RUN.json and the manifest of rows with their parts, in the run folder
aa_plan.waits: SchwingNet PR 483 (the flow and the plans); the PREREG frozen

job: each trial job builds them once, cached
aa_rows.title: Crops
aa_rows.short: A box around every vertebra, centred on its mask.
aa_rows.does: Cuts one crop per labelled vertebra around the mask's centroid, top down, with no landmark oracle. 48 x 56 x 32 voxels at 2 mm. Shares the volume rows with a person key that your stage 4 reads; my crops are whole columns, your three-body windows are yours.
aa_rows.reads: the CTs and label maps (NIfTI) on the grid
aa_rows.writes: a crop cache named by each row's digest, so a rerun reads it back
aa_rows.waits: bordercall PR 40 (frame=centroid), vendored at afe1952 on PR 483

aa_trial.title: Train one schedule
aa_trial.short: 50 epochs of the fully latent network under one anneal schedule.
aa_trial.legend: New drawing, the anneal: a strip of four small panels of what the privileged branch sees as lambda rises, (1) the target vertebra's mask, (2) every vertebra's mask, (3) both blurred, (4) a soft threshold of the CT; under it w, that branch's weight, falling from 1 to 0. Beside it four tiny curve pairs over training: lambda-then-w (lambda rises over 15-55 percent of the steps, w falls over 45-85), joint (both over 15-55), w-first (w over 15-55, lambda over 45-85), and the null, flat at lambda 1 and w 0.
aa_trial.does: Trains objective=mask: the decoder gives the privileged mask channels back and a name head reads the bottleneck, with no measurement anywhere. Only the anneal varies between arms. The null never anneals: it reads the CT alone from step 0, so it is the network with no privileged information. Then evaluates on the validation persons.
aa_trial.reads: the training crops; the trial's words (schedule, seed)
aa_trial.writes: the trial's ledger entry (final validation Dice, mean surface distance in mm, name accuracy), its per-epoch curve, the checkpoint, the latent vector of every validation crop
aa_trial.jobnote: An epoch is ceil(training CTs / batch) steps at batch 2 whole spines, so 48 steps; 50 epochs is 2,400 steps. The anneal spans the whole run.

aa_join.title: Compare with the null
aa_join.short: Does any anneal schedule beat no anneal at all?
aa_join.does: Gathers the 8 ledger entries. A schedule beats the null when both its seeds' final validation surface distance sit below both null seeds'. Plots every trial's curve. A trial that failed is shown failed, never dropped.

aa_report.title: Report
aa_report.short: Plots with short notes, and the CLAIM report.
aa_report.does: Writes the CLAIM and REFORMS report from the run folders, plots first.
aa_report.writes: the report under the run folder

placement: Beside your stage 4, independent of your stages 1 to 3: it needs no export, no PDM and no head block. It shares the volume rows with a person key. Its question is the anneal schedule with the head held at F; yours is the head with the schedule held.

decisions.card: Start with a fully latent approach: objective=mask, no measurement in the loss.
Short 50-epoch runs, as many in parallel as possible, each trial its own GPU card.
The question is whether the annealer helps, so the arms are the anneal schedules and the null never anneals.
decisions.why: greg asked to evaluate the annealer's performance; a null with no privileged information is the only fair yardstick.
8 cards in one array; the decision needs every seed of an arm to beat every null seed, so one seed cannot pass by luck.

decisions.card: ENHANCE.PET CTs only, 96 training and 24 validation.
decisions.why: One label scheme, and 1,558 of the store's 1,733 gold 3 rows (1,725 of them allowed for training); a short run that answers in hours. VerSe and TotalSegmentator join the full run.

decisions.card: The naming term is off; the name head stays on.
decisions.why: The naming term needs every spine to have the same count of crops, and real columns differ. The name head reads each crop alone.

decisions.card: JAX 0.10.2 and Flax 0.12.8 on the grid.
decisions.why: The grid's training environment is Python 3.11, which the newest JAX does not support; bordercall's 86 tests pass on these versions.
